---
title: "Battlegrounds: the close contests"
subtitle: "Eight state-level snapshots · scenario data, not live polling"
description: "Illustrative Senate and House battleground margins and campaign finance comparisons."
---

The map is a mix of statewide Senate contests and competitive House districts. The figures below are **synthetic scenario inputs** designed to show how to compare races: they are not actual polls, campaign disclosures, or official Cook Political Report ratings. “Rating” is a Cook-style label for this demonstration only.

## Margin and uncertainty

The dot is the scenario's Democratic two-party margin; positive values favor the Democratic candidate. The horizontal interval shows an assumed ±4-point uncertainty band, not a poll's published margin of error.

```{r}
#| label: battleground-data
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)

battlegrounds <- tribble(
  ~state, ~race, ~office, ~dem_candidate, ~rep_candidate, ~margin, ~uncertainty, ~dem_funds, ~rep_funds, ~rating,
  "PA", "PA-07", "House", "Democratic candidate", "Republican candidate", 1.5, 4.0, 5.2, 6.1, "Toss-up",
  "MI", "Senate", "Senate", "Democratic candidate", "Republican candidate", 2.0, 3.8, 24.0, 21.5, "Toss-up",
  "WI", "WI-03", "House", "Democratic candidate", "Republican candidate", -1.0, 4.2, 3.8, 4.7, "Lean R",
  "AZ", "AZ-01", "House", "Democratic candidate", "Republican candidate", 0.5, 4.1, 4.5, 5.0, "Toss-up",
  "GA", "Senate", "Senate", "Democratic candidate", "Republican candidate", -0.5, 4.0, 19.0, 22.0, "Toss-up",
  "NV", "NV-03", "House", "Democratic candidate", "Republican candidate", 1.0, 4.3, 5.0, 4.4, "Toss-up",
  "NC", "Senate", "Senate", "Democratic candidate", "Republican candidate", -2.0, 4.0, 17.0, 23.0, "Lean R",
  "OH", "Senate", "Senate", "Democratic candidate", "Republican candidate", -3.0, 4.2, 15.0, 26.0, "Lean R"
) |>
  mutate(
    race_label = paste(state, race, sep = " · "),
    dem_share = 50 + margin / 2,
    total_funds = dem_funds + rep_funds,
    funding_leader = if_else(dem_funds >= rep_funds, "Democratic", "Republican"),
    hover = paste0(
      race_label,
      "<br>Combined scenario funds: $", round(total_funds, 1), "m",
      "<br>Modeled Democratic share: ", round(dem_share, 1), "%",
      "<br>Democratic funds: $", dem_funds, "m",
      "<br>Republican funds: $", rep_funds, "m"
    )
  )

margin_chart <- plot_ly(
  data = battlegrounds,
  x = ~margin,
  y = ~reorder(race_label, margin),
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers",
  color = ~office,
  colors = c("Senate" = "#c7473a", "House" = "#187f78"),
  error_x = list(
    type = "data",
    array = battlegrounds$uncertainty,
    visible = TRUE,
    color = "#7b8794",
    thickness = 1.5,
    width = 5
  ),
  marker = list(size = 12),
  text = ~paste0(
    race_label,
    "<br>Scenario Democratic margin: ", if_else(margin > 0, "+", ""), margin, " pp",
    "<br>Assumed uncertainty: ±", uncertainty, " pp",
    "<br>Illustrative rating: ", rating
  ),
  hoverinfo = "text"
) |>
  layout(
    xaxis = list(title = "Democratic two-party margin (percentage points)", zeroline = TRUE, zerolinecolor = "#243b53"),
    yaxis = list(title = NULL),
    legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = 1.12),
    margin = list(l = 120, t = 25),
    hovermode = "closest"
  ) |>
  config(displayModeBar = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)

margin_chart
```

## Fundraising and modeled vote share

Each point is a race. The horizontal axis combines both candidates' scenario fundraising totals; the vertical axis translates the assumed margin into a Democratic two-party vote share. A larger combined fundraising total does not imply a closer race or a causal effect on vote share.

```{r}
#| label: fundraising-scatter
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
fundraising_chart <- plot_ly(
  data = battlegrounds,
  x = ~total_funds,
  y = ~dem_share,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers",
  color = ~rating,
  colors = c("Toss-up" = "#c7473a", "Lean R" = "#187f78"),
  text = ~hover,
  marker = list(size = 15, line = list(color = "white", width = 1)),
  hoverinfo = "text"
) |>
  layout(
    xaxis = list(title = "Combined candidate fundraising (illustrative $ millions)"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Modeled Democratic two-party vote share (%)", range = c(45, 55)),
    legend = list(title = list(text = "Illustrative rating")),
    margin = list(t = 20),
    hovermode = "closest"
  ) |>
  config(displayModeBar = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)

fundraising_chart
```

::: {.source-note}
All margins, uncertainty bands, fundraising totals, modeled shares, and ratings in these charts are fabricated for demonstration. State/race labels identify plausible contest types; candidates are intentionally unnamed. Fundraising is in illustrative millions of dollars, with no claim about actual receipts or disbursements.
:::

## Scenario inputs

| State | Example contest | Rating label | Scenario margin |
|:--|:--|:--|--:|
| Pennsylvania | PA-07 (House) | Toss-up | +1.5 pp |
| Michigan | Senate | Toss-up | +2.0 pp |
| Wisconsin | WI-03 (House) | Lean R | −1.0 pp |
| Arizona | AZ-01 (House) | Toss-up | +0.5 pp |
| Georgia | Senate | Toss-up | −0.5 pp |
| Nevada | NV-03 (House) | Toss-up | +1.0 pp |
| North Carolina | Senate | Lean R | −2.0 pp |
| Ohio | Senate | Lean R | −3.0 pp |

These are a teaching dataset, not a ranking. A serious race comparison should date each poll and finance report, distinguish candidate committees from outside spending, and document the rating source.
